response.text:
Following the convention: keep INV_ID 690 (paid, and also first entered), void INV_ID 801, and reverse every line of journal 2467 (the journal that recorded the voided copy) in an open period.

Journal 2467 lines: 5200 DR 16634.31 and 2000 CR 16634.31. The reversal swaps sides: 5200 CR 16634.31, 2000 DR 16634.31. Open periods are 11 and 12; journal 2467 is in period 8, which is closed, so the reversal must post to an open period. I'll use period 11 (the earliest open period).

Note the instruction says to reverse the journal that recorded the voided copy with corrects_jrnl_no set to that journal, so corrects_jrnl_no = 2467.

arguments.reasoning: F003: Invoice V0020-84200-690 is recorded twice for vendor V0020 with the same date (20240813) and amount (16634.31). INV_ID 690 (journal 2130) is paid (P) and was entered first, so it is kept. INV_ID 801 (journal 2467) is an open duplicate (O) and is voided (status V). Journal 2467 recorded the voided copy, so its two lines (5200 DR 16634.31 / 2000 CR 16634.31) are fully reversed in this correction, referencing corrects_jrnl_no 2467. The reversal posts to open period 11, because period 8 is closed. The original and reversal net to zero, and the reversal balances on its own. Only INV_ID 801 is changed, and the status change is permitted because this is a duplicate_invoice finding. Note that INV_NO for 801 has leading spaces; this is a normalisation issue and does not affect the decision.
